plain: The system where partners and AWS log the deals they're working on together.
real: If it isn't in ACE, as far as AWS is concerned it didn't happen.

plain: Did the partner bring the deal to AWS, or help close one AWS already had?
real: Who gets credit. This is usually why the meeting ran long.

plain: Custom pricing for a specific customer, bought through AWS Marketplace instead of a separate contract.
real: The customer can use money they've already committed to spend with AWS, which is usually the whole point.

plain: An AWS badge confirming a partner has proven expertise in a specific area.
real: Months of paperwork and customer references, and the thing that gets you invited to certain meetings.

plain: A partner's sales team and AWS's sales team working the same deal together.
real: Two comp plans pointed at one customer. It either works great or not at all.

plain: Market Development Funds. Money from AWS to pay for marketing that partners do together with them.
real: It comes with paperwork and a deadline, and it expires whether you use it or not.

plain: The one sentence explaining why a customer should buy both products together.
real: Usually written by committee, so it ends up three sentences long. (I have written several.)

plain: We'll talk about it after this call.
real: Someone on this call shouldn't hear the answer.

plain: One of the giant cloud providers: AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud.
real: The three companies whose roadmaps everyone else plans around.

plain: The AWS portal where partners manage their AWS relationship, including deals, training, funding, and listings.
real: Where the work gets recorded, which isn't always where it happens.

plain: Model Context Protocol. A standard way to connect an AI agent to a tool or data source, kind of like a universal adapter.
real: The plumbing that decides what an agent can actually touch, which makes it a security question.

plain: AWS's online store, where customers buy software through their existing AWS account and bill.
real: Procurement's favorite shortcut, because the contract already exists.

plain: Software Composition Analysis. Tools that list the open source components in an application and flag ones with known vulnerabilities or license issues.
real: It tells you which of the 900 libraries you didn't write is going to ruin your quarter.

plain: The automated pipeline that builds, tests, and ships code every time a developer makes a change.
real: The conveyor belt. Security tools either ride it or get skipped.

plain: Software Development Lifecycle. The whole path from writing code to running it in production.
real: Every team says they have one. Ask who approves the exceptions.

plain: Whether a company's cloud is set up safely, like who has access, what's exposed to the internet, and what's misconfigured.
real: Almost always worse than people assume. (Usually by a lot.)
